questions.q: The correct decreasing order of dipole moment of the methyl halides is:
questions.explain: μ = q × d. Fluorine gives the largest charge but over a very short C–F bond (139 pm), so CH₃Cl (1.860 D) edges out CH₃F (1.847 D); from Cl to I the charge falls faster than the bond lengthens.

questions.q: Which of the following has zero dipole moment?
questions.explain: In the trans isomer the two equal C–Cl bond dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel. The cis and ortho isomers and CHCl₃ all have a net dipole.

questions.q: Arrange CCl₄, CHCl₃, CH₂Cl₂ and CH₃Cl in increasing order of dipole moment.
questions.explain: The more chlorines spread round the tetrahedral carbon, the more their bond dipoles cancel: CCl₄ (0) < CHCl₃ (about 1.1 D) < CH₂Cl₂ (about 1.6 D) < CH₃Cl (about 1.9 D).

questions.q: If a single C–Cl bond dipole in chlorobenzene is μ₁, the dipole moments of o-, m- and p-dichlorobenzene (using 2μ₁ cos(θ/2)) are approximately:
questions.explain: The angles between the dipoles are 60°, 120° and 180°, so 2μ₁cos30° ≈ 1.7μ₁, 2μ₁cos60° = μ₁ and 2μ₁cos90° = 0, giving ortho > meta > para.
